description: MCP/CLI outcome: relay plan run <planId> --budget 3m --findings. Runs the Plan (or the daily subset that fits the budget, longest-pole cases deferred and listed), waits for completion or budget, then produces the Findings markdown with an agent-proposed verdict and reason per item (using the judge artifacts and before/after evidence). close_reason: iOS locale sweeps now compare the app instead of the keyboard. Proven on a real 3-locale iPad sweep: 30 findings/28 keyboard/0 real defects became 5 findings/0 keyboard/2 real defects, including the untranslated pt-BR composer string the analyzer had missed.
description:
The 3-locale iPad sweep (batch f3430b2e) captured 19 controls on the Ask screen, and none of them belong to Grok.

pt-BR ask-screen stableKeys, all 19:
  id:systeminputassistantview, id:centerpageview   (typing predictions bar)
  Ciao / Non / Ma                                   (prediction candidates)
  id:rightbuttonbar, id:delete, id:return, id:shift, id:more, key[22..24], button[2]
  structure:application[0]                          ("Bernardo Ferrari, SuperGrok")
  label:application:grok                            ("Buscar")

The screenshot of that same frame is full of Grok in Portuguese -- "Criar videos", "Editar imagem", "Modo Voz", "Abrir camera", "Pergunte qualquer coisa", "Fale". None of it is in the tree. The iOS keyboard is presented, and the accessibility snapshot returns the keyboard hierarchy rather than the app's content beneath it.

Two consequences, and the second is the expensive one:

1. Every finding the sweep produced is keyboard noise. The keyboard follows the system keyboard language, not Grok's, so those labels are identical across locales and every one is reported as untranslated. That is 28 of the 30 findings.

2. It missed a real defect that is plainly visible in the screenshots. Grok's composer shows "Esperto" in Italian and "Expert" in pt-BR -- an untranslated string, exactly the class of defect this whole pipeline exists to find. The analyzer could not see it because the control was never in the tree.

So the sweep is currently comparing the wrong app's UI. Screenshots are good; trees are not. Fixing this matters more for 40x40 than throughput does -- 1600 cases of keyboard labels is worse than not running it.

Likely fix is to dismiss the keyboard before the body screenshot rather than to change the snapshot: the recipe body for grok-ios-settings-shot is launch-and-screenshot, and Grok opens with the composer focused. A tap on "Hide keyboard" / "Nascondi tastiera" is itself locale-dependent, so prefer a non-semantic dismissal.

Repro: node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs packages/cli/src/index.ts job locale-matrix start --input '{"recipe":"grok-ios-settings-shot","serial":"db0c9b7c3aeb83dc2259d08e3b521a30f621d3f5","profileId":"grok-ios","locales":["en","it"]}' then read the frame-observation artifacts in runs/*_<batchId>_*/run.json.
design:
Root cause is not a wrong-app capture. The snapshot is the app's own tree, complete: a live Grok Ask capture on the iPad is 149 nodes and contains the missed string ("Expert", node 142, Button, identifier toolbar.model.selector.button). The tree was fine. corpusControls threw the app away.

Three mechanisms, in order of damage:

1. hittable is meaningless on an iOS XCTest tree. Of 149 live nodes, 44 are hittable, and every one of them is either the Application/Window/frame chain or the software keyboard. Not one Grok control is hittable -- AGENTS.md already warns that large SwiftUI cells report hittable:false.

2. actionableAnchor climbs to the nearest hittable ancestor, so for every Grok control that ancestor is the application frame. corpusControls then takes BOTH the stableKey and the tap target from the anchor rather than the node. Every control on the screen therefore gets the application's identity, and the `seen` dedupe on stableKey collapses all of them into one. That is the whole bug: a 179-node iOS Settings tree produced exactly 2 controls, both of them the root under two different keys.

The keyboard was never captured "instead of" the app. It was the only thing that survived the collapse, because iOS keyboard keys are real UIKit views: individually hittable, each with its own identifier, so each kept a distinct identity. 17 of the 19 reported controls were keyboard; the other 2 were the collapsed app root.

3. isSystemOrKeyboardNode only knew Android IME package names, so iOS keyboard subtrees were never excluded in the first place.

Measured, replaying the real stored trees from batch f3430b2e through corpusControls:
  before: 179 nodes -> 2 controls (both the app root)
  after:  179 nodes -> 33 controls, one per translatable Settings row
Live Grok Ask tree (149 nodes):
  before: 19 controls, 17 keyboard, "Expert" absent
  after:  4 controls, 0 keyboard, "Expert" present as id:toolbar.model.selector.button

Fix, in packages/core/src/snapshot-app-content.ts (new) and corpus-screen-analysis.ts:
- An anchor must be a row, not the screen. Application/Window, and any container filling the app frame, can no longer lend identity to a control. The frame area is read from the Application element, never from "the largest rect", so a scoped or single-row snapshot still works.
- The software keyboard is excluded by subtree, reusing the logic screen-identity already had for fingerprints (moved to the new module, so there is one definition). RightButtonBar was missing next to LeftButtonBar and is now covered.
- Anchor-derived identity is kept where the anchor is a genuine row, so Android's row/subtitle collapse is unchanged.

Keyboard dismissal was measured and deliberately not adopted: dismissing it on the Ask screen took the tree from 149 to 99 nodes and produced the identical 4 app controls. The filter alone is sufficient, and it is robust whether or not a text field happened to take focus. Adding a dismiss step to the sweep body would only add a failure mode.

Separately found and fixed while measuring that: structural keys were not stable across keyboard presence (application[0]/other[3] with the keyboard up vs other[2] with it down), because the keyboard is hosted in an unlabeled full-frame shell that renumbers the app's own containers. Two locales that disagreed about focus would have reported one row as one control vanishing and another appearing. Ordinals are now counted over nodes that carry content -- ones with a label, value, or identifier, or an ancestor of one -- so a row keys the same either way. Verified on the two real captures.
notes:
Fixed and proven on the physical iPad db0c9b7c3aeb83dc2259d08e3b521a30f621d3f5, server :8787, RELAY_ACTOR_ID=agent:grok-mapper.

Real 3-locale sweep, batch 6534cc98-7076-4d17-a2cc-361513270188 (en, it, pt-BR, restore en). All four cases passed: 53s, 55s, 69s, 53s.

Findings, comparing against the pre-fix sweep f3430b2e on the same recipe and the same three locales:

  before: 30 findings, 28 of them the iOS keyboard, 0 real Grok defects, and the visible "Expert" defect missed
  after:   5 findings, 0 keyboard, 2 distinct real Grok defects, "Expert" among them

The five, all on the authored ask-screen:
  pt-BR  "Expert" is unchanged from en        <- the defect this bead was filed for
  it     "Photo Edit" is unchanged from en    x2
  pt-BR  "Photo Edit" is unchanged from en    x2

id:toolbar.model.selector.button now reads Expert / Esperto / Expert across en / it / pt-BR, keyed identically in all three, so the analyzer sees that Italian translated it and Brazilian Portuguese did not. That is the comparison the pipeline exists to make, and it is the first time it has worked on iOS.

Coverage went from "12 of 28 frames" to 4 of 4. The matrix wrapper brackets each body with its own screenshots, captioned "locale:<x> before body" / "after body", and the authored-frame filter only knew the "before · " / "after · " shape a tap uses. So the wrapper's frames were analyzed as content: "before body" is the iOS Settings language list, which compared Apple's UI and the language endonyms against themselves for 30 of the 40 findings an intermediate measurement showed, and "after body" is the authored screen again, reporting every real finding twice. Both are now excluded by one predicate shared by the analyzer and the pack export, which previously disagreed with each other depending on whether the batch declared an expected screenshot count.

The device was left as found: the restore case returned it to English.

Tests: packages/core/src/snapshot-app-content.test.ts (9) covers keyboard subtree exclusion, flattened trees, the frame-vs-row anchor rule, the no-frame-element case, layout-only containers, the collapse regression, the Esperto/Expert comparison, and key stability across keyboard presence. One added to locale-run.test.ts for the wrapper frames. 883 core tests pass.

description:
The pipeline is proven at 3 locales x 1 screen on a physical iPad (batch f3430b2e, agent-device-vly). 40x40 is 1600 cases; what is now known to stand between here and there:

1. Wall clock. The 4-case sweep took 3m30s, about 52s per case, because entryPath reruns iOS Settings navigation for every case. At that rate 1600 cases is 23 hours. The screens dimension is the cheap one to batch: one language switch should drive a whole tour of screens, not one screenshot. Measure before optimizing -- the switch itself is only part of the 52s.

2. Findings volume. 3 locales x 1 screen produced 30 findings, most of them noise that is honest but not the app's (iOS system keyboard, account name). Linear scaling puts 40x40 in the tens of thousands. The known-findings triage store keys on CorpusFinding.id, which is derived from code/screen/locale/control, so accepting a defect in one locale does not quiet it in the other 39. Deciding whether acceptance should be per-locale or per-control is a product question, not a bug.

3. Restore cost. Every matrix appends a restore case. Harmless at 4, one wasted case per test at scale.

4. Frames without trees. analysisCoverage on the real pack read 12 of 28. The other 16 are the before/after pairs around each tap, which are correctly not analyzed, but the README line "Frames read: 12 of 28" invites the reader to think 16 frames were missed. Worth wording as authored-vs-incidental.

Not blocking: the language switch itself is reliable now, the analysis reads real trees, and both analysis and export survive a server restart and the 100-job registry cap.

description: Separate AI proposals from deterministic policy for may-execute, auto-approve, reject, ask-human, and insufficient-evidence decisions, then project results to GitHub checks and human reports.

Output is may-execute plus approve|reject|human|insufficient-evidence with stable rule ids, reasons, evidence refs, confidence only where policy permits, and unresolved verification. AI can propose classifications but cannot mutate policy or approved source. verify-change composes diff impact, representative pilot, affected expansion, evidence comparison, first causal failure, and this exact policy decision.

design:
# Decision: trusted-process Device membrane is sufficient

Date: 2026-08-20
Status: accepted
Applies to: SpaceXAI trusted-studio use of Relay (local desktop/CLI/MCP against owned devices)

## Threat model

Relay already wraps adapters in `createDeviceObservationFacade` (`packages/core/src/device-observation-membrane.ts`). That facade is an in-process capability boundary:

- Public `Device` values expose observation only.
- Mutation goes through canonical helpers that own exact-once dispatch.
- The source adapter is stored in a `WeakMap`, not on the public object.
- Tests can inject named doubles without reaching raw transport.

It is **not** a security sandbox. Same-process code can still:

1. Import a private adapter module and call it directly.
2. Mutate an adapter before it is wrapped.
3. Use Node `child_process` / `net` to talk to adb, go-ios, or XCTest outside Relay.
4. Read workspace evidence (screenshots, AX trees, serials) from `.relay/` and `runs/`.

Attacker classes that matter:

| Attacker | In scope today? | What they can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Honest authoring / QA code that accidentally calls `tap` from a read path | Yes | Membrane blocks this at the public Device value |
| Malicious npm dependency or untrusted plugin loaded into the Relay process | Not a supported product surface | Full process compromise: device control, evidence theft, lease theft |
| Separate CLI/MCP actor on the same trusted host | Yes | Project roles, leases, and exact-once mutation already gate this |
| Remote untrusted tenant | No | Relay is not multi-tenant SaaS |

SpaceXAI's current use is a trusted studio: operators and in-house agents run a local Relay against devices they own. Plugins/adapters are first-party. There is no public plugin marketplace and no untrusted script execution inside the Relay process.

## Decision

Keep the trusted-process Device membrane. Do **not** build a process/worker RPC layer now.

Rationale:

- Exact-once mutation and canonical dispatch live in one process on purpose. Splitting them across an RPC boundary without a product need would add a second mutation owner and create silent retry / dual-dispatch risk.
- A worker that still imports `device.ts` in the same Node process would not change the threat model.
- A real process boundary is required only if Relay later loads untrusted plugins or third-party adapters into the runtime. That product does not exist.

## When to reopen

Reopen this decision if any of the following land:

1. A plugin/adapter API that executes third-party JavaScript inside Relay.
2. A hosted multi-tenant control plane where tenants share a Relay process.
3. Untrusted recipe/script evaluation that can import Node modules.

The then-required design:

- Plugin worker process with no raw adb/go-ios/XCTest handles in plugin memory.
- Canonical dispatch and exact-once mutation remain in the trusted host.
- Observation-only RPCs for plugins; mutations are requested as typed intents and executed once by the host.
- Explicit test doubles stay at the host membrane, not inside plugin workers.

Until then, process isolation would be unused infrastructure and a source of hidden retries.
notes: Recorded decision 2026-08-20: trusted-process Device membrane is sufficient for SpaceXAI trusted-studio use. Process/worker RPC is required only if untrusted plugins or shared-process multi-tenant adapters land. No RPC layer built.
title: Evaluate process-isolated Device transport for untrusted adapters

close_reason:
Fixed in packages/core/src/recipe-runner-app.ts. openAppAndVerifyForeground now separates 'nobody can say who owns the screen' from 'somebody else does'. Android still fails closed on an unavailable observation because captureAndroidForegroundApp names the resumed activity, so silence there means the helper is broken. iOS logs 'this target cannot say which app owns the screen, so the step is not verified' and continues, which matches AGENTS.md ('XCTest is optional', 'do not fail a tour only because the tree is missing'). A handoff still fails: the mismatch branch is untouched, so Grok to iOS Settings still reports the app it landed on.

Two new tests in recipe-runner-app.test.ts cover the iOS continue and the iOS mismatch; the four existing tests including the Android fail-closed case still pass.

Verified on the device, not just in tests: before the fix, three locale-matrix cases died at step 3 of 3 with 'app open: expected ai.x.GrokApp in foreground after 2 attempts; observed unavailable' (batch ccbcae08). After the fix, the same recipe's app-open and sleep steps report ok on batches ad9f7004, 92e7f1fe and 78588fed, and failures moved downstream to real tap problems.
description:
openAppAndVerifyForeground fails closed when it cannot observe which app owns the screen. On Android that is right — captureAndroidForegroundApp reads the resumed activity, so 'unavailable' means the helper is broken. On iOS the observation comes from node.bundleId in the XCTest tree, and this iPad's tree carries none: a snapshot returns 149 nodes with labels and types and no bundle ownership at all. So the observation is 'unavailable' on a device where Grok is demonstrably in the foreground, and every recipe whose first step is 'app open' dies before its second step.

Found while dogfooding agent-device-vly on iPad db0c9b7c…: jobs 9e65f955 and db6090da both died with 'app open: expected ai.x.GrokApp in foreground after 2 attempts; observed unavailable' while a screenshot showed SuperGrok's Ask composer. That blocks the locale matrix on iOS entirely, so it blocks the 40x40 goal on the iPad.
title: Every iOS recipe fails at app open: the tree carries no bundle ownership

close_reason: Closed
description:
compareLayoutCost() reads crossings, then bends, then siblingMovement, then routeDistance. Because it is strictly lexicographic, a single removed corner justifies any amount of sibling reordering, and there is nothing that says how much reordering a corner is worth.

Measured on grok-hand (19 screens, a crawl, so recorded order is visit order) while shipping agent-device-yrm:
- before: crossings 0, bends 16, siblingMovement 0
- after:  crossings 0, bends 12, siblingMovement 5

The pair-packing rule did not reorder anything itself — a shelf lays its children out in the order it is given. It changed the geometry enough that a promotion the optimizer had always been allowed to make became the cheaper arrangement. So the change is inside the existing contract; the contract is the seam.

Five inversions is one parent's five children read in almost the opposite order from the order somebody tapped them. Four corners is a small tidying. The trade reads wrong even though every step of it is what the comparator says.

Options, none obviously right:
- A budget: a bend improvement only outranks movement while movement stays under some count, which needs a defensible count.
- Weigh them: bends and movement in one term, which gives up the lexicographic reading the comparator's doc is written around.
- Scope it: movement outranks bends for graphs whose order is a recorded walk (a crawl), and not for hand-arranged maps. Relay knows which is which.

Wants a human eye on the grok-hand render before and after, the same way agent-device-ckc was decided.
notes:
Fixed by giving the trade a budget, at the place the promotion is accepted rather than inside the comparator: compareLayoutCost stays strictly lexicographic and keeps its doc, and layoutPrimaryForest now refuses an alternative that moves siblings more than SIBLING_MOVEMENT_BUDGET = 1 further out of recorded order unless it removes a crossing.

Why one: one inversion is two siblings swapping, the smallest disagreement an arrangement can have with the order somebody walked the app in, and the pair still reads as the same list. Five is one parent's five children read almost backwards, and no amount of corner tidying is worth telling that story. A crossing is exempt, which is the same reason the comparator puts crossings first.

The "scope it to recorded walks" option was tried first and abandoned: Relay does not actually know which is which at layout time. The canonical Connection has no provenance field (CanvasTransition has one, the canonical document does not), so the only crawl signal reaching layout is the observed:discovery-... id namespace, and app-map-projection.ts states outright that ids must never decide visual reading order. sourceAnchor is the one recorded-order evidence layout gets, and it is already respected by the hasRecordedSourceOrder guard. Scoping honestly would mean adding provenance to the protocol and the import path — worth doing one day, too big for a comparator fix.

Measured on every live map on the local server (.tmp-measure/cost-compare.mts):
- grok-hand: inversions 6 -> 1, bends 8 -> 12, shape 3760x1490 -> 3760x1850, so fit against a 2:1 pane 79.3% -> 98.4%. Keeping the walk order made the map read better AND arrive bigger.
- every other map byte-identical, including grok-settings (44 screens), grok-android-manual-v2 (41 screens, 29 crossings) and android-settings-v3 (the yrm fit win).
Rendered before/after with the walk step number on each card: /tmp/relay-review/budget-before.png and budget-after.png. Before, the hub's children read 17, 10, 2, 3 — the last thing recorded drawn as the first branch. After they read 2, 3, then 4..14, then 10, 17.

The previous agent's single-swap promotion is deliberately still allowed: the cross-link test at app-map-auto-layout.test.ts:646 pays exactly one inversion for two corners and still passes. New test "will not read a fan backwards to straighten a cross-link" is the same graph with two more earlier siblings, so the promotion would cost four; it fails if the budget is raised, so it is not vacuous.
title: A layout may reorder siblings without limit to buy one fewer corner

description:
Mission
Make Relay a proof-first device automation system that can validate, simulate, diagnose, and repair as much as possible without a connected device. A connected device becomes final acceptance evidence, not the place where correctness is first discovered.

Product invariants
1. Frozen raw pixels + accessibility evidence are the source of truth for offline compile/preflight/replay.
2. Every physical mutation is exact-once. A timeout, disconnect, cancellation-after-dispatch, or unknown native outcome is terminal and produces a durable review package; it never triggers a hidden fallback, Back, cleanup, relaunch, retry, or second tap.
3. Every App Map Test execution has a typed immutable intent: compiled plan, recipe graph/root digests, selected runtime profile, and successful frozen-evidence preflight. No route may control a target before validating it.
4. Observation is shareable and independent from exclusive input. iOS pixels remain useful when XCTest/AX is slow, in-flight, stale, or unavailable.
5. Origin restoration, full-surface capture, and navigation use evidence-bound state transitions only. No geometry/title/heuristic claim can mint a proof.
6. Dynamic/private data surfaces (for example Shared Conversations) are classified as dynamic and are exercised for behavior, not brittle visual diffs.

Breaking-change policy
Prefer one explicit safe contract over compatibility shims. Legacy App Map Test jobs without a valid scoped intent must stop with a structured migration/review result. Generic App Map Test Combine/campaign routes remain blocked until they can bind and preflight each exact cell. Do not infer Test identity from recipe strings or opaque artifacts.

Workstreams and Beads
A. Scoped offline Test contract — complete: agent-device-uah, agent-device-uah.1. Main commits f6d3d8b86, d9cf93dd2, 6fd1965b9. Global runtime-profile ledger; immutable raw variant provenance; UI/CLI/MCP profile selection; server preflight before discovery/lease/control/enqueue; Combine/campaign legacy entrypoints fail closed.
B. Reexecution intent gate — active P0: agent-device-1og, folding agent-device-x81. Carry/revalidate typed App Map Test intent through job retry, POST /jobs retryOf, run replay, resume, and repair retry before control; preserve intent artifacts.
C. Combine cell model — open P1: agent-device-bfz. Add explicit evidence profile/preflight per Test cell before re-enabling Combine/campaign execution.
D. Offline simulator/replay/cursor firewall — maintain and extend e1o/c3r.19 paths. Validate selectors, cursor/return states, schedule, current matcher, causal failure chain, and read-only repair proposal entirely from frozen plan/evidence.
E. Full-surface state machine — active: agent-device-yji (physical final acceptance) and agent-device-dxs (reviewed-origin bootstrap). Native capture proof is preferred; reviewed Android top-origin authority is a separate signed/revocable sidecar, never a mutable capture field.
F. Exact-once iOS and transport truth — retain and ratchet the terminality suite across all mutation paths. Pixels/MJPEG are independent of XCTest; AX timeout/in-flight is distinct from runner failure; stage controls expose preview/labels/input truth. Hardware proof remains separately tracked.
G. Architecture and product UX — maintain small named seams, public observation-only Device facade/runtime membrane, explicit state-machine diagnostics, compact accessible Evidence/run controls, clear repair actions, and no hidden retries. Future security boundary: agent-device-6f0.
H. Device-only acceptance — after offline gates are green, execute Android map Test (40 logical surfaces) with verified startup/cached rerun performance, fresh full Voice/Settings/SuperGrok captures, dynamic Shared Conversations behavior handling, Kids cleanup/back drill, and iPad preview/AX timing validation. Device observations may close acceptance beads but may not weaken offline invariants.

Sequence
1. Finish B and integrate/review it.
2. Finish reviewed-origin authority (E) and its UI review affordance.
3. Run static simulator/contract/architecture gates.
4. Build Combine per-cell scope (C).
5. Run controlled hardware acceptance only when a target is connected; collect durable evidence and create repair work for any mismatch.
6. Use measured results to optimize cold/warm Test execution without removing proof steps.

close_reason:
Took the calm option: below the zoom where a dash pattern's marks cover a screen pixel, the dash is dropped and the edge paints as one quiet hairline. edgeDashesRead() in connection-presentation.ts, tested; wired through connectionStrokeClass with props.viewportScale.

The evidence that decided it came from agent-device-rog rather than from staring at the two renders. Widening the shelf makes a fan of siblings sit side by side at exactly one parent-child gap, and the only thing that says they are siblings and not a chain is the corridor their edges arrive along -- an elbow over the top of the row rather than a straight line from the card to their left. So at Fit the rail's job is structural, and an unbroken hairline does that job better than a comb of sub-pixel dashes. Draft still reads as draft on colour, which has no minimum size.

Thresholds are derived per pattern from the token rather than picked: draft is 4 canvas units on, so it resolves to 0.25; return is 2, so it goes at 0.5. EDGE_DASH_SHORTEST_MARK mirrors --map-edge-dash-*, and tokens.css now points back at it.

Not done: the "running" state keeps its 7 4 dash at every zoom. It is animated and transient, and nothing in the evidence said to touch it.

Before: /tmp/relay-review/xok6-rails-crop.png. After: /tmp/relay-review/ckc-after-rails.png.
description:
Asked for as a cheap win alongside xok.6 and deliberately not taken, because the evidence does not say which direction is the improvement and a guess here is a coin flip on the map's whole character.

What is actually painted at Fit (14%): every crawl edge is 'needs-recording', so it is dashed --map-edge-dash-draft (4 5) at stroke-width 2 in canvas units. Nothing compensates for scale, so on screen that is a 0.28px line with 0.5px dashes — the pattern is below a pixel and paints as a faint fuzzy rail. Magnified evidence: /tmp/relay-review/xok6-rails-crop.png (3x crop of the Automations corridor at Fit). Whole view: /tmp/relay-review/xok6-after-fit.png.

Two coherent treatments, opposite in spirit:
- Calm: below a reading zoom, drop the dash and paint one quiet hairline. Nothing is lost because the dash is already unreadable there, and the shimmer goes. Risk: a draft edge stops looking draft, leaving only colour (--map-edge-draft vs --map-edge-ready) to carry it.
- Honest rhythm: scale the dasharray by 1/zoom so a draft edge keeps its designed on-screen dashes at every zoom. Risk: a fitted map of 33 draft edges becomes an explicit dashed comb — busier, which is the thing that prompted the ask.

Both are a few lines in connectionStrokeClass in app-map-canvas-scene.tsx (props.viewportScale is already there). Needs a human eye on the two renders before either lands.
title: Corridor rails at Fit: decide whether they calm down or hold their rhythm

close_reason:
Fixed in three places, so a name can neither be born on top of a card nor lifted into one.

1. packages/core/src/app-map/canvas-slots.ts (new) — canvasSlotAllocator hands out the next geometrically free lattice slot for newly observed screens. Both accept paths in observation-proposal.ts previously derived a slot from an index they each owned alone (position in a proposal, or the map's screen count), so a second crawl filed its screens directly on top of the first crawl's. A slot's reserved area is card + label band, and occupancy is measured geometrically, so a screen somebody has since dragged keeps its space. This is the root cause of the stacks on the real map.

2. Shared canvas geometry now names the band. app-map-screen-layout.ts exports SCREEN_LABEL_HEIGHT, MAX_LABEL_COUNTER_SCALE, SCREEN_LABEL_BAND, screenLabelBounds() and CARD_PITCH_X/Y. The tidy-tree vertical pitch is derived from the band rather than a hand-tuned gap, and the renderer's counter-scale cap comes from the same constant, so the layout and the renderer cannot drift. app-map-label-rows.ts additionally refuses to lift a name onto a row where the counter-scaled band would enter a frame it does not label.

3. packages/app/src/lib/app-map-destack.ts (new) — resolveCoincidentPositions repairs maps already carrying stacks. Two cards at the same point are never an arrangement somebody made: one screen is hidden, unclickable, its name on top of its neighbour's. Only exactly-coincident screens move, only the ones after the first, and only to the first whole slot clear of every other card's reserved area. Applied where the canvas reads saved positions (app-map-canvas-geometry.ts), not where it writes them, so the repair commits the first time somebody drags the freed card and a deliberate arrangement of merely-close cards is untouched.

Verified on the real 44-screen default:grok-settings map in the running app: 44 cards rendered, 0 coincident pairs, 0 headers overlapping a frame they do not label. Before: 3 coincident pairs (Ara/Settings 2 of 5, Connectors/Settings 3 of 5, Screen 4 of 5/Screen 5 of 5).

Tests: app-map-destack.test.ts (5), plus 'reserves the name band above every card on a dense map' in app-map-auto-layout.test.ts and the lift guard in app-map-label-rows.test.ts. No CSS hacks; everything is measured at the most zoomed-out reading, so it holds at any zoom.
description: On the 44-screen Grok Settings map the auto-layout stacks 'Ara' on top of 'Settings 2 of 5' near the bottom of the graph, so one frame's title sits inside another's card. The disambiguating qualifier makes this more visible, not less, because two overlapping frames now both carry a 'n of m' suffix. Layout needs to reserve the label band, not just the card.

acceptance_criteria: A control with a stable identifier is either compared in every locale or in none, and a sweep whose baseline is not English produces the same set of compared controls as one whose baseline is.
close_reason:
Chrome is now a property of the control, not of its copy. corpusControls decide skipCrawl from the accessibility identifier (profile chromeIdentifiers + a locale-invariant identifier shape) or from a LocalizedStringKey; the English word list is only the fallback for trees with no stable name. Chrome is still recorded so a sweep can compare "Search"/"Cerca", just never opened.

Pinned by test "chrome is filtered by identifier, so every locale is compared equally": the Ask screen that used to yield 4 controls in en and 10 in it now yields the same stableKey set in both, with Search/sidebar/Attach/Speak observed and skipCrawl, and the Ask/Build tabs kept as destinations.

Live 3-locale iPad sweep ed96f4c1 (en/it/pt-BR) after the fix: 12 controls on ask-screen in every locale. Re-analysis of that batch found 11 real findings vs 5 on the pre-fix 6534cc98 pack — including untranslated "New Message" (id:ask.toolbar.textfield) that the English word list had been hiding. Zero keyboard noise. Agent died during vp check after the proof; corpus.test.ts 23/23 pass.
description:
Found while proving agent-device-2xr on a real 3-locale iPad sweep (batch 6534cc98). Now that iOS controls actually reach the analyzer, the sweep shows the baseline locale being filtered harder than the locales compared against it.

Same screen, same recipe, same identifiers, one sweep:

  en     ask-screen: 4 controls
  it     ask-screen: 10 controls
  pt-BR  ask-screen: 10 controls

The six that only appear outside English, by identifier and by what each locale called them:

  id:sidebar.search.field      Search / Cerca / Buscar
  id:navigation.tab.ask        Ask / Chiedi / Pergunte
  id:navigation.tab.build      Build / Compilazione / Construir
  id:sidebar.open.button       Open sidebar / Apri la barra laterale / Abrir barra lateral
  id:ask.toolbar.add.button    Attach / Allega / Anexar
  id:voice.speak.button        Speak / Parla / Fale

corpusControls drops chrome by matching the visible label against an English word list (isExploreChromeLabel in explore.ts, plus the app profile vocabulary in discovery-app-profiles.ts). "Search" and "Open sidebar" match; "Cerca" and "Abrir barra lateral" do not. So the filter is a function of the language the screen happens to be in.

The damage is quiet, which is why it needs filing rather than watching. These six are not reported as findings -- the analyzer compares a control against the same key in the baseline, and the baseline does not have them, so they are skipped in every locale. Six real, translatable Grok controls are therefore never compared in any of the 40 languages, and no finding says so. Coverage reads 4 of 4 frames inspected, which is true and still hides this.

It can also fire the other way: a locale whose translation happens to collide with an English chrome word gets that control dropped in that locale only, which does surface, as a control that exists in 39 languages and vanished in one.

Fix direction: chrome is a property of the control, not of its copy. Every one of the six carries a stable identifier. Deciding chrome on identifier -- or on the baseline's verdict for that key, applied to every locale -- makes the filter locale-independent either way. The label list can stay as the fallback for trees with no identifiers, but it must not be the thing that decides whether a locale gets compared.

Not a regression: the same vocabulary was there before agent-device-2xr. It could not be seen, because the anchor collapse meant almost no iOS control reached the filter at all.
title: Chrome filtering is keyed on English labels, so the baseline locale is compared less than the other 39

Across nine real maps the median fit zoom is +73% and no map is worse than before. The two largest crawls move most: grok-android-manual-v2 9.0% -> 20.5% (+128%), grok-settings-ipad 24.1% -> 47.2% (+96%). android-settings-crawl and grok-hand are unchanged.

Levers, each tested on its own:
- Loose band wrapping: rejected with data, and it needed no change. It already wraps at max(4, occupiedColumns), so widening the shelf carried it from 3 rows of 7 to 2 rows of 10 for free. Forcing it wider than the journey measured -10%.
- MAX_SHELF_COLUMNS 4 -> 7: the knee. 5 and 6 are identical to 4 on the 14-item Settings fan; 8 and above overshoot grok-settings-ipad into a width-bound strip.
- MIN_SHELF_ITEMS 5 -> 3, not 2. See agent-device-yrm: the last step is worth another 20% on two maps and switches off the primary-branch optimizer.

Two bugs found by measurement, both fixed here:
- subtreeColumns counted chain depth rather than placed width, so a subtree one row tall that packs leaves side by side under-reserved columns and the next side path landed on top of it. Real card overlap on grok-android-manual-v2 and grok-settings-ipad. It now mirrors place(). It does not move the shipped layout: every 4/5 measurement is identical before and after.
- The local optimizer was re-sorting shelf rows narrowest-first to shave route distance, quietly rewriting the order somebody recorded their taps in -- against the promise siblingLayoutGroups already makes. compareLayoutCost now ranks siblingMovement above routeDistance: a crossing or a corner outranks recorded order, a few pixels of edge length does not. Cost: grok-hand holds at baseline instead of gaining 34%.

Still height-bound, and honestly so. Width binds grok-settings at 38% and it fits at 15%, so there is headroom left; the remaining levers are agent-device-yrm and the shelf-overshoot seam noted there. The xok.6 side-path invariant still holds -- its test now compares side paths against the journey rather than against one named card, because the shelf, not the packing, is what sets the width.
description:
After root-band packing (xok.6) the tidy default:grok-settings map is 2360x4990, aspect 0.473. A 1440x716 canvas is aspect 2.0, so Fit is limited by height and lands at 12-14%: the cards occupy roughly the middle quarter of the window and the rest is grid. Screenshot: /tmp/relay-review/xok6-after-fit.png.

Every remaining lever is a width lever, and each is a real design decision rather than a tweak:
- The loose band wraps at max(4, occupiedColumns) = 7 columns, so 18 edgeless captures spend 3 rows. Nothing can be misread inside that band — it is already an admitted grid of screens with no path — so it could wrap at whatever width balances the map instead of at the journey's width.
- MAX_SHELF_COLUMNS is 4, deliberately 'about as wide as it is tall so one fan cannot push the rest of the journey off the canvas'. The 11-child Settings fan therefore spends 4 rows. A wider shelf trades that guarantee for a map that fits.
- MIN_SHELF_ITEMS is 5, so a fan of three (two leaf Asks plus Automations) stays a column and spends two nearly empty rows beside a tall sibling. The rule that a small fan 'arrives whole on one screenful' is written for reading zoom, not for Fit.

Do not raise all three at once. Measure each against .tmp-measure/roots.mts (height, aspect, fit zoom) and against whether the fan still reads as the list it was recorded from.
notes:
Shipped MAX_SHELF_COLUMNS 4->7 and MIN_SHELF_ITEMS 5->3, plus two fixes the widening exposed.

Measured with .tmp-measure/sweep.mts (2D grid over both constants, 9 real maps, fit zoom at 1440x716).

Levers, tested individually:
- Loose band wrapping: REJECTED with data. It already wraps at max(4, occupiedColumns), so it follows the journey width for free -- widening the shelf took it from 3 rows of 7 to 2 rows of 10 with no code change. Forcing it wider than the journey overshoots into a width-bound strip (-10%).
- MAX_SHELF_COLUMNS: 4->7 is the knee. 5 and 6 are identical to 4 on the 14-item Settings fan (3 rows); 8+ overshoots grok-settings-ipad into aspect 5.6 and costs median fit.
- MIN_SHELF_ITEMS: the dominant lever, and the expensive one. 5->3 keeps every deep contract. 5->2 is worth another +50% on grok-settings but breaks 13 tests including the primary-branch/cross-link optimizer, because a fan of two collapses onto one row and "which branch owns the parent row" stops meaning anything. Filed separately.

Two real bugs the widening exposed and this change fixes:
1. subtreeColumns measured chain depth, not placed width, so a subtree one row tall that packs leaves side by side reserved too few columns and the next side path was laid on top of it. Real overlaps on grok-android-manual-v2 and grok-settings-ipad. Now mirrors place(). Does not perturb the shipped 4/5 layout at all -- every baseline number is identical before and after.
2. The local optimizer was re-sorting a shelf narrowest-first to save route distance, silently rewriting recorded tap order -- against siblingLayoutGroups' own promise that "the order the actions were recorded in stays exactly the order the shelf reads in". compareLayoutCost now ranks siblingMovement above routeDistance: a crossing or a corner outranks recorded order, a few pixels of edge length does not.

Cost of fix 2: grok-hand returns to baseline fit instead of +34%. Honest trade.

description: A physical iOS interaction is advertised as one bounded XCTest operation, but packages/core/src/device.ts routes press, scroll, and type commands through controlled, whose default retry policy repeats transient errors up to three times. packages/core/src/workspace-interact.ts wraps this in withSession and can also run pixel verification, so one intended tap can produce repeated native mutations before the outer proof sees a pixel change. This can duplicate a toggle, dismiss a sheet, or move to a later screen while diagnostics still claim one session attempt. The runner must distinguish idempotent read retries from irreversible device mutations and surface every retry decision as attributed evidence.
design: For physical iOS, make mutating XCTest operations single attempt by default: point and semantic press, swipe or pan, text, key, back or home, clipboard, settings, and video control. Do not infer that a transport timeout means the action did not occur. Preserve retry only behind an explicit reviewed idempotency and verification contract that records before and after evidence plus an operation level retry record. Keep bounded query and read behavior separate. Ensure withSession diagnostics report native action attempts, not only the outer session wrapper. Do not alter Android raw input behavior in this slice.
notes: Integrated exact-once iOS mutation safety as main 70c8559e0: all physical iOS mutations get one native attempt; uncertain outcomes require evidence-backed intervention, and semantic-to-point fallback is only for proven selector misses. title: Make physical iOS mutations exactly once and report retry decisions

description: `captureDeviceVideo({ action: "start" })` calls `ensureIosRunnerPrepared(target.device, serial)` with the default `allowHostRepair: true`. acceptance_criteria: 1. Native AX timeout has a distinct typed/result code from missing XCTest session and includes bounded elapsed time plus in-flight state. 2. description: `snapshotIosSingleFlight()` times out a physical iOS accessibility request after 8 seconds, but `snapshot()` then maps every `/timed out/` error to `"iOS snapshot needs an active XCTest session"`. `workspace-capture` diagnoses that as a runner/session-unavailable condition, records semantic control unavailable, and points people toward Reconnect even while the uncancellable native tree traversal is still correctly retained in the single-flight guard. A slow/full SwiftUI tree is therefore misreported as a dead runner and can trigger needless repair behavior instead of a truthful pixels-still-live / AX-in-flight state.
notes: Integrated as main 14efd8222. Exact-once mutation policy is preserved. Full core/protocol/app tests, typecheck, app build, and vp check passed.
title: Classify slow iOS AX snapshots as in-flight latency, never missing XCTest

acceptance_criteria: 1. Relay pins a known-safe producer revision or uses a maintained local sidecar with bounded latest-frame delivery, cancellation-safe consumer removal, and no send-on-closed-channel race. 2. Source shutdown/reconnect and a stalled upstream client are soak-tested without process crash, unbounded goroutines, or orphan source process. 3. Stage reports measured source and delivered FPS/frame age; it never advertises a target FPS that Instruments screenshot polling cannot prove. 4. Any alternate `ui stream` provider is an explicit reviewed architecture choice and does not silently add DeviceKit/WDA control paths.
description: Relay currently launches `ios screenshot --stream` as its live iPad pixel source. The vendored go-ios Instruments implementation (`vendor/go-ios/ios/instruments/screenshot.go`) captures PNGs sequentially, decodes/re-encodes them, then starts an unbounded goroutine per consumer per frame to send on an unbuffered channel; the handler closes that channel on disconnect. A disconnect racing an outstanding sender can panic with send-on-closed-channel, while a slow consumer accumulates blocked goroutines. The source also exposes no FPS contract. Relay protects its own downstream fanout, but cannot make this upstream producer reliable or 60fps by itself.
notes: Integrated safe sidecar as main b7151b3d4 and built it locally at .relay/bin/relay-ios-preview (version relay-ios-preview/1, pinned go-ios ebec9a0b076c). It replaces unsafe go-ios screenshot --stream with one bounded pixels-only pipe; Go race soak, vet, build/version and Relay package gates passed. No DeviceKit/WDA/XCTest/control path.
title: Pin or replace unsafe go-ios Instruments MJPEG producer before relying on it for iPad live preview

acceptance_criteria: Accepting a finding records whether it applies to one locale or to that control in every locale, geometry-derived codes cannot be accepted across locales by default, and an everywhere acceptance carries a note.
close_reason: Closed
description:
Product decision, carved out of agent-device-43e item 2 so the scale work is not blocked on it.

Today acceptance is keyed on CorpusFinding.id, which is derived from code, screen, control and locale. Accepting a defect in Italian leaves the identical defect open in the other 39 languages.

The store is not the obstacle. markLocaleFindingKnown (locale-finding-triage.ts:47) already persists code, canonicalKey, screenLabel, stableKey and locale next to the id; only the match is keyed on the id. Widening it is a small change once the intent is settled.

Recommendation: the answer is per code, not global, because the two families of finding do not generalize the same way.

- Text-identity codes (POSSIBLE_UNTRANSLATED_TEXT). The real sweep reports "Photo Edit" unchanged from English in both Italian and Brazilian Portuguese. If a reviewer decides Photo Edit is a product name that is deliberately never translated, that is one fact about one string, true in all forty languages. Making a human record it forty times is how a reviewer learns to stop reading findings.
- Fit and geometry codes (POSSIBLE_TEXT_CLIPPED and anything derived from a rect). German overflowing a button says nothing about Japanese in the same button. Accepting across locales here would hide real defects.

So: offer the scope at accept time -- this locale, or this control everywhere -- defaulting by code, and record the chosen scope on the stored row so the reason survives. A note is already supported and should be required for the everywhere scope, since that is the one asserting something about languages nobody looked at.

Leaving it as-is is also defensible while the sweep is 3x1. It stops being defensible at 40 locales, where one accepted brand name costs 39 more decisions.
notes: Completed in commit c79b803f (isolated branch; to be integrated). Locale is the backward-compatible default. Cross-locale control scope is allowed only for POSSIBLE_UNTRANSLATED_TEXT with stableKey and required reason; geometry/layout findings cannot generalize. Full protocol/core/server/CLI/MCP/app suites, monorepo typecheck, vp check/test green.
title: Decide whether accepting a locale finding accepts it for the other 39

description: Relay reserves a durable run-test workflow before app-map.test.run so a lost enqueue response can be reconciled. When the server returns a known pre-dispatch rejection (for example HTTP 409 TARGET_PROFILE_SELECTION_REQUIRED), the workflow facade currently converts it into mutation-outcome-unknown and leaves an active workflow with no job/resource. description:

A crawl produces several disconnected roots — the main Settings journey plus a tail of small ones whose screens are titled Back / Screen / Ask — and each root gets its own full-width horizontal band, so the fitted map is a column of blocks with empty canvas between them.

Two directions, both presentation-only and both inside the tidy/unarranged path:
- Pack roots the way siblings are now packed: a short root is a one-row subtree, so the same shelf rule could wrap the tail of small roots into a block instead of a band each.
- Or treat them as a different kind of thing: an unreachable/orphan tail is arguably not a journey and could be filed under a labelled area rather than laid out as one.

Prefer the first if it lands cheaply — it is the rule already in app-map-auto-layout.ts applied one level up, since roots are siblings of a virtual entry. The second is a product decision about whether orphan screens deserve a journey shape at all, and should not be made silently by a layout tweak.
notes:
Shipped as root-band packing in packages/app/src/lib/app-map-auto-layout.ts (rootBands()).

Decision on the product question: orphan/short roots keep their real shape and their real edges; nothing invents a group, a label, or an edge. What changed is only which band they sit on. A root whose whole subtree is at most MAX_SIDE_PATH_ROWS (2 rows plus the gap between them) is a side path — a couple of screens the crawl reached from a state it never came back into. Side paths pack left to right under the taller roots, in observed order, with SIDE_PATH_GUTTER_COLUMNS (1) of empty canvas between two of them so the pair cannot read as one continuing path. Two guards keep it honest and keep old maps still: packing may never make the map wider than its widest journey already is (so a narrow map of short paths still reads one path per row — the memory/storage test still passes untouched), and if no band ends up holding two roots the original observed order is used unchanged rather than reordered for nothing. A declared flow entry is never demoted to a side path. Edgeless captures still go to the existing loose band below everything.

description:
agent-device-rog widened the shelf (MAX_SHELF_COLUMNS 4->7) and lowered the floor for packing a fan (MIN_SHELF_ITEMS 5->3). Lowering that floor one more step, to 2, is the single largest remaining width lever, and it was deliberately not taken.

Measured (fit zoom at 1440x716, .tmp-measure/sweep.mts):
- grok-settings           14.9% -> 17.8%  (aspect 0.865 -> 0.930)
- grok-android-manual-v2  20.5% -> 22.5%
- grok-settings-ipad, grok-hand, android-settings-v3, android-settings-crawl: unchanged

So it is worth roughly another 20% on the two largest crawls and nothing anywhere else.

What it costs: 13 tests in app-map-auto-layout.test.ts, against 7 for the 5->3 step, and the extra six are a different kind. At a floor of 3 the failures are all one thing -- recorded order now reads across a row instead of down a column -- which is honestly restated with readsBefore(). At a floor of 2 the primary-branch tests go too: "uses local connector geometry to promote the branch that removes a cross-link", "keeps a direct continuation on its parent row despite a same-rank cross-link". A fan of two is the commonest shape in a map, and packing it side by side means there is no longer a parent row for a branch to win, so the local layout optimizer has nothing to choose between. That is a real capability being switched off, not an assertion needing a rewrite.

There is also a shape argument, weaker but real: two cards side by side at one parent-child gap are exactly a screen and the screen it opens, and the corridor is the only thing saying otherwise. Three or more at least look like a row.

Needs a human eye on a render of a two-fan map at reading zoom before deciding, the same way agent-device-ckc did.

Related seam, cheap to fold in: a shelf can overshoot. android-settings-v3 (5 screens) tidies to 5 columns by 1 row, aspect 7.1, which flips the map from height-bound to width-bound -- still better than baseline (43.7% -> 75.8%) but short of the 83.7% a 3x2 would give. A per-shelf aspect target was tried and measured worse overall (+39% median against +73%) because it optimizes each shelf's shape rather than the map's, so it was dropped. A cap that only bites once the map is already wider than it is tall might get both.
notes:
Shipped, both halves, without a blanket MIN_SHELF_ITEMS=2.

A fan of two packs only when one of its two sides is a dead end (packsAsPair, app-map-auto-layout-shelves.ts). The reason a pair was held back was the local branch optimizer: it removes a cross-link by promoting one of a parent's branches onto the parent's own row, and packing both onto a shelf leaves no primary row to win. But that is only a choice when both sides continue — a branch that opens nothing carries nothing onto the row it would be promoted to, so promoting it was never the move that removed anything. So the pair that had something to lose keeps a row each, and the pair that did not, packs. Both capabilities coexist; nothing was switched off. It is also the pair that reads worst packed that stays unpacked: one card beside a longer chain is plainly a row, while two chains starting side by side leave the corridor doing all the work of saying so.

The overshoot seam folded in, and it is the same idea in the other direction. MAX_SHELF_COLUMNS became a default of 7 that every branch is still arranged against, plus a set of widths (3..10) the settled arrangement is re-flowed at, picking whichever leaves the map nearest the proportion it is read in. Choosing the width AFTER the optimizer has settled which branch owns which row is the whole trick: a re-flow can only fold rows into each other, it cannot hand the step above a cheaper route and quietly swap two siblings to reach it. Chosen without that ordering, widening reordered a pair on grok-android-manual-v2.

Measured, fit zoom at 1440x716, against live maps (.tmp-measure/session.mts), both changes against the state at the start of the session:

  map                     screens   before       after        fit%          gain   siblingMovement
  grok-settings                44   3400x3930    3400x2890    14.9 -> 20.1   +35%   0 -> 0
  grok-android-manual-v2       41   3400x2830    3760x2170    20.5 -> 26.5   +29%   3 -> 4
  grok-hand                    19   2360x2570    3760x1490    22.5 -> 34.3   +52%   0 -> 5
  android-settings-v3           5   1640x230     940x610      75.8 -> 83.7   +10%   0 -> 0
  grok-settings-ipad           17   2700x1010    2700x1010    47.2 -> 47.2     0%   0 -> 0
  android-settings-v2/crawl    11   unchanged                 40.2 -> 40.2     0%   0 -> 0
  3-screen and 1-screen maps                                 100.0 -> 100.0    0%   0 -> 0

android-settings-v3 lands on exactly the 83.7% this bead predicted a 3x2 would give. No map got worse on any measure.

Two maps moved siblings. Neither was moved by packing — a shelf lays its children out in the order it is given, and recorded anchors are still skipped outright. Both were the existing optimizer taking a promotion that the new geometry made cheaper: grok-android-manual-v2 bought a crossing and two corners for one inversion, grok-hand bought four corners for five. The first is a fine trade, the second is not, and the reason it is allowed is that compareLayoutCost puts bends above siblingMovement lexicographically with no budget. Filed as agent-device-9aj rather than fixed here, because changing that ordering is a change to the honesty contract and wants a human eye.

Also filed agent-device-xgd: the width is chosen for the pane's proportion and cannot know the map already fits, so a tiny map is re-shaped for a zoom it will never be drawn at.

Two added: one pins re-flowing wider on a height-bound map, one pins wrapping narrower rather than lying out in a strip. Shelf logic moved to app-map-auto-layout-shelves.ts to stay inside the source budget. pnpm verify green.
title: A fan of two still spends two rows, and it is the last big width lever
